::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING contract

This page is the single current candidate authority for SCNSim V1 component
authoring. Its classes, signatures, and docstrings are now importable as a
fail-fast scaffold; physical validation, compilation, and execution are not
yet implemented, accepted, stabilized, or released.
:::

## Reading goal

Use one route from reusable component definitions to a sealed physical Plan:

```text
immutable Library
-> component instances with exact source identity
-> named nets and one node-flux reference
-> ports on named nets
-> CircuitPlan
```

The `CircuitPlan` remains the only physical authority. A schematic, compiled
backend row, reduced view, or solver result is evidence derived from that Plan,
not another circuit definition.

This page owns the product-facing Library and component API. The
[V1 Runtime Contract](v1-runtime-contract.qmd) owns Plan sealing, Ref lineages,
Direct/HB execution, Results, receipts, and resolution.

## One Library model

Built-in and custom catalogs are immutable `Library` objects imported directly:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitPlan, library as sc, units as u
from my_components import library as custom

plan = CircuitPlan(id="example")
```

Every component instance carries the exact library name, version, source, and
component-schema identity that created it. SCNSim does not provide string-based
component discovery, a Notebook-global registry, or a mutable
`CircuitLibrary.register_component(...)` workflow.

Built-in and custom components use the same authoring surface:

```python
readout_cap = plan.add(
    sc.capacitor(
        id="readout_cap",
        capacitance=92.0 * u.fF,
    )
)

fixture = plan.add(
    custom.fixture(
        id="fixture",
        coupling_capacitance=8.0 * u.fF,
    )
)
```

`plan.add(library.component(...))` is the only component-creation route.
There are no convenience methods such as `plan.capacitor(...)` that could
become a second catalog or parameter authority.

### Pins and public parameters

Electrical terminals are addressed only by declared pin names:

```python
readout_cap.pin("a")
readout_cap.pin("b")
```

Consumer-visible parameters are addressed only through the component's public
schema:

```python
capacitance = readout_cap.parameter("capacitance")
```

A composite may contain primitive children, but child IDs and child parameters
are inspection evidence, not automatically a consumer API. The factory must
deliberately expose every supported `ParameterRef`. This keeps refactoring an
internal expansion from silently changing Notebook contracts.

Custom libraries publish the same immutable `Library` object, use
`scnsim.units`, and declare the same pin, public-parameter, and lowering
evidence. V1 does not add a second unit registry or a global plugin mechanism.
The Python mechanism used to implement a custom factory is package work that
follows this outward contract; it is not a second Notebook UX.

## Named electrical topology

### Create a net once

One call creates one named node and assigns all of its pins:

```python
plan.net(
    "signal_node",
    coupling_cap.pin("b"),
    resonator.pin("signal"),
)
```

The node ID is unique within the Plan. All pins belonging to that node are
supplied together; repeated pairwise `connect()` calls are not the primary
authoring model and cannot incrementally redefine a sealed net.

### Declare one node-flux reference

Each Plan declares exactly one reference node:

```python
plan.reference(
    "ground",
    input_cap.pin("a"),
    pump_inductor.pin("b"),
)
```

The call may contain no external pins:

```python
plan.reference("ground")
```

This zero-pin form still gives grounded composites the unique node-flux
reference they require. It does not create an implicit second ground inside
each component.

### Bind ports to nets

Ports refer only to existing named nets:

```python
plan.add_port(
    id="signal_in",
    at="signal_node",
    role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)
```

A port is not a Library component and cannot bind an arbitrary component pin.
It adds an external excitation/observation boundary to a named circuit node.
The port role and reference impedance remain explicit, Quantity-checked Plan
data.

## Built-in leaves

All public physical parameters are SCNSim-registry Quantities. R/L/C/JJ leaves
use the fixed pins `"a"` and `"b"`.

| Factory | Public physical parameters | Additional public reference | Realization |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resistor` | `resistance` | none | one R branch |
| `capacitor` | `capacitance` | none | one C branch |
| `inductor` | `inductance` | `inductive_branch("self")` | one linear L branch |
| `josephson_junction` | `josephson_inductance`, `junction_capacitance=0 * u.F` | none | nonlinear JJ plus optional parallel C row |

```python
r = plan.add(sc.resistor(id="loss", resistance=2.0 * u.kohm))
c = plan.add(sc.capacitor(id="shunt", capacitance=90.0 * u.fF))
l = plan.add(sc.inductor(id="coil", inductance=1.2 * u.nH))
j = plan.add(
    sc.josephson_junction(
        id="junction",
        josephson_inductance=320.0 * u.pH,
        junction_capacitance=2.0 * u.fF,
    )
)
```

`josephson_inductance` always means the per-junction small-signal
`L_J0` at the stable zero-phase, zero-bias operating point. It is also the
parameter from which the HB backend obtains the nonlinear Josephson
constitutive strength. SCNSim does not interpret it as an arbitrary
bias-point inductance.

A nonzero `junction_capacitance` lowers as an independent capacitor in parallel
with the ideal Josephson element. Exact `0 * u.F` records that this model omits
the capacitor. SCNSim never estimates `Cj` from `Lj`, and adding `Cj` does not
add resistance or turn the component into an RCSJ model. The canonical physics
is documented in
[Josephson Current, Phase, Energy, and Inductance](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/josephson-physics/josephson-current-phase-energy-and-inductance.qmd#independent-parallel-junction-capacitance).

## General composites

### Scalar RLGC transmission line

`transmission_line` accepts one immutable `ScalarRLGC` value and expands a
uniform scalar line into a fixed ladder. Model authors can declare that value
directly:

```python
from scnsim import ScalarRLGC

rlgc = ScalarRLGC(
    resistance_per_length=0.2 * u.ohm / u.m,
    inductance_per_length=410.0 * u.nH / u.m,
    conductance_per_length=0.0 * u.S / u.m,
    capacitance_per_length=165.0 * u.pF / u.m,
)

line = plan.add(
    sc.transmission_line(
        id="feedline",
        length=4.0 * u.mm,
        rlgc=rlgc,
        n_sections=40,
    )
)
```

Or they can load the same typed value from one solver-native AEDT Q2D combined
`CG, RL` matrix CSV:

```python
from scnsim import load_q2d_scalar_rlgc

rlgc = load_q2d_scalar_rlgc(
    "results/q2d/rlgc_matrix.csv"
)

line = plan.add(
    sc.transmission_line(
        id="feedline",
        length=4.0 * u.mm,
        rlgc=rlgc,
        n_sections=40,
    )
)
```

These are two creation routes for the same `ScalarRLGC` contract, not two
transmission-line factories or two compiler paths. `transmission_line` does not
also accept the four per-length values as parallel keyword arguments. When a
compatible SCGSim Q2D Result exposes the native export as `primary_csv`, that
`Path` may be passed directly to `load_q2d_scalar_rlgc`; SCNSim neither runs
AEDT nor imports PyAEDT.

The V1 loader accepts only one scalar signal mode: each primary Capacitance,
Conductance, Inductance, and Resistance matrix must occur exactly once, have
the same single conductor label, and be `1 x 1`. The native header must identify
the combined `CG, RL` problem, per-length units, and a finite extraction
frequency. Values must be finite, with positive `L'` and `C'` and nonnegative
`R'` and `G'`. Optional native coupling or Spice-output blocks do not replace
the four primary matrices.

A multiconductor export fails closed. Selecting one diagonal entry would
silently discard mutual terms and would not produce the declared scalar mode.
The Q2D reference-conductor name is not inferred from the primary matrix label;
the imported scalar shunts bind to the `CircuitPlan`'s one declared reference.

The loader normalizes values through `scnsim.units` and preserves the source
format, file-content SHA-256, extraction frequency, conductor order, original
units, and parsed canonical values as provenance. A machine-local path is only
an authoring input and is not the computational identity. Loading a raw CSV
does not claim that a SCGSim receipt, AEDT version, adaptive convergence, or
reference identity was verified.

The imported values are frozen scalar coefficients at their recorded
extraction frequency. SCNSim applies them across the requested circuit solve
grid without interpolation or a broadband-material claim. A future
frequency-dependent or multiconductor line requires a separate accepted model;
it must not change `ScalarRLGC` by inference.

Its pins are `"head"` and `"tail"`. `n_sections` is a fixed positive Python
integer, not a physical Quantity or optimization variable. The bound length is
divided by that fixed count for each ParameterSet; optimizing length changes
the section length but never changes the discrete topology or matrix rank.
V1 does not imply multiconductor or frequency-dependent RLGC behavior.

The lowering is one canonical pi ladder. For
`dx = length / n_sections`, each section has series `R' * dx` followed by
series `L' * dx`; `C' * dx / 2` and `G' * dx / 2` are shunted to the Plan
reference at each section boundary. Adjacent sections therefore accumulate
their two half shunts at an internal node. For exact zero R, the resistor
endpoints are contracted so the section remains a pure series-L branch; exact
zero G omits the shunt-conductance branch. Both cases preserve the declared
section-boundary grid and `n_sections`, but receipts still record the actual
primitive rows and internal-node realization.

The continuum-to-ladder physics and refinement obligation remain canonical in
[Telegrapher Model: From RLGC Continuum to a Finite LC Ladder](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/transmission-lines/telegrapher-rlgc-distributed-line.qmd#finite-symmetric-pi-section).

### Interdigitated capacitor

`interdigitated_capacitor` preserves the complete two-terminal lumped
capacitance model:

```python
idc = plan.add(
    sc.interdigitated_capacitor(
        id="coupler",
        terminal_1_to_reference_capacitance=18.0 * u.fF,
        terminal_2_to_reference_capacitance=21.0 * u.fF,
        terminal_mutual_capacitance=7.0 * u.fF,
    )
)
```

Its pins are `"terminal_1"` and `"terminal_2"`. The expansion contains
`C_1G`, `C_2G`, and `C_12`; it does not collapse all three into one series or
mutual capacitor. Both ground branches bind the Plan's unique reference.

### Finite-loop symmetric SQUID

`symmetric_squid` is an explicit two-junction finite-loop component:

```python
squid = plan.add(
    sc.symmetric_squid(
        id="squid",
        josephson_inductance=310.0 * u.pH,
        junction_capacitance=2.0 * u.fF,
        loop_inductance=45.0 * u.pH,
    )
)
```

Its pins are `"terminal_a"` and `"terminal_b"`. Both junction rows share the
same public `josephson_inductance` `ParameterRef` and the same public
`junction_capacitance` `ParameterRef`; V1 does not expose per-arm overrides.
Both values are per-junction values, so the expansion contains two equal
Josephson rows and, when nonzero, two equal parallel `Cj` rows.
The exact oriented expansion is:

```text
J1 || Cj1 : terminal_a -> terminal_b
L_loop    : terminal_a -> loop_node
J2 || Cj2 : loop_node   -> terminal_b
```

`loop_node` is private inspection evidence, not a public pin. `L_loop` is the
finite loop self-inductance and is addressable as
`squid.inductive_branch("loop")` with the shown orientation. This is the
executable finite-loop topology, not the negligible-loop effective-cosine
surrogate.

The physical distinction and branch conventions are canonical in
[DC SQUID Flux Tunability](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/josephson-physics/dc-squid-flux-tunability.qmd#finite-loop-mutually-pumped-dc-squid).

## Six resonator factories

SCNSim exposes six explicit factories rather than one topology enum or an
ambiguous `parallel_lc_resonator`:

| Grounding | Branch | Factory | Pins |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grounded | linear L | `grounded_parallel_linear_lc_resonator` | `signal` |
| Floating | linear L | `floating_parallel_linear_lc_resonator` | `terminal_a`, `terminal_b` |
| Grounded | one nonlinear JJ | `grounded_parallel_single_junction_resonator` | `signal` |
| Floating | one nonlinear JJ | `floating_parallel_single_junction_resonator` | `terminal_a`, `terminal_b` |
| Grounded | finite-loop symmetric SQUID | `grounded_parallel_symmetric_squid_resonator` | `signal` |
| Floating | finite-loop symmetric SQUID | `floating_parallel_symmetric_squid_resonator` | `terminal_a`, `terminal_b` |

Grounded variants bind their internal return to the Plan reference. A linear
factory exposes `inductance`; a single-junction factory exposes
`josephson_inductance` and `junction_capacitance`; a SQUID factory exposes
`josephson_inductance`, `junction_capacitance`, `loop_inductance`, and
`inductive_branch("loop")`.

Grounded factories use one `subsystem_capacitance` from `signal` to reference.
Floating factories instead require all three subsystem branches:

- `terminal_a_to_reference_capacitance`;
- `terminal_b_to_reference_capacitance`; and
- `terminal_mutual_capacitance`.

For a nonlinear resonator these subsystem capacitances remain separate from
the junction's own parallel `junction_capacitance`. Composite expansions do
not publish `branch1`, `branch2`, arbitrary child injection, or a generic
topology selector.

### Grounded linear example

```python
from scnsim import CircuitPlan, library as sc, units as u

plan = CircuitPlan(id="grounded_linear")

input_cap = plan.add(
    sc.capacitor(id="input_cap", capacitance=6.0 * u.fF)
)
resonator = plan.add(
    sc.grounded_parallel_linear_lc_resonator(
        id="readout",
        subsystem_capacitance=110.0 * u.fF,
        inductance=5.8 * u.nH,
    )
)

plan.reference("ground")
plan.net("input", input_cap.pin("a"))
plan.net("readout_node", input_cap.pin("b"), resonator.pin("signal"))
plan.add_port(
    id="signal_in",
    at="input",
    role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)
```

### Floating linear example

```python
floating = plan.add(
    sc.floating_parallel_linear_lc_resonator(
        id="floating_mode",
        terminal_a_to_reference_capacitance=52.0 * u.fF,
        terminal_b_to_reference_capacitance=47.0 * u.fF,
        terminal_mutual_capacitance=16.0 * u.fF,
        inductance=7.0 * u.nH,
    )
)

plan.net("island_a", floating.pin("terminal_a"))
plan.net("island_b", floating.pin("terminal_b"))
```

The two terminal-to-reference capacitances are real branches even though the
component has no ground pin. They bind the Plan's one declared reference.

### Single-junction examples

```python
grounded_jj = plan.add(
    sc.grounded_parallel_single_junction_resonator(
        id="grounded_jj",
        subsystem_capacitance=85.0 * u.fF,
        josephson_inductance=420.0 * u.pH,
        junction_capacitance=2.5 * u.fF,
    )
)

floating_jj = plan.add(
    sc.floating_parallel_single_junction_resonator(
        id="floating_jj",
        terminal_a_to_reference_capacitance=41.0 * u.fF,
        terminal_b_to_reference_capacitance=39.0 * u.fF,
        terminal_mutual_capacitance=14.0 * u.fF,
        josephson_inductance=420.0 * u.pH,
        junction_capacitance=2.5 * u.fF,
    )
)
```

The two factories share the JJ model contract; only their capacitive subsystem
and external pins differ.

### Finite-loop SQUID flux-pump example

The pump coil is an ordinary Plan component. Mutual coupling refers to exact
oriented inductive branches, while drive current belongs to an HB case:

```python
from scnsim import (
    CircuitPlan,
    CircuitRun,
    CurrentDrive,
    HBCaseSpec,
    HBTruncation,
    HBSolveSpec,
    PumpAxis,
    library as sc,
    units as u,
)

plan = CircuitPlan(id="flux_pumped_resonator")

jpa = plan.add(
    sc.grounded_parallel_symmetric_squid_resonator(
        id="jpa",
        subsystem_capacitance=95.0 * u.fF,
        josephson_inductance=300.0 * u.pH,
        junction_capacitance=2.0 * u.fF,
        loop_inductance=40.0 * u.pH,
    )
)
pump_inductor = plan.add(
    sc.inductor(id="pump_coil", inductance=1.0 * u.nH)
)

plan.reference("ground", pump_inductor.pin("b"))
plan.net("signal", jpa.pin("signal"))
plan.net("pump_drive", pump_inductor.pin("a"))
plan.add_port(
    id="signal",
    at="signal",
    role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)
plan.add_port(
    id="pump",
    at="pump_drive",
    role="terminated",
    reference_impedance=50.0 * u.ohm,
)

plan.couple_inductive(
    id="flux_pump",
    inductor_a=jpa.inductive_branch("loop"),
    inductor_b=pump_inductor.inductive_branch("self"),
    coupling_coefficient=0.98 * u.dimensionless,
)

run = CircuitRun(plan=plan, workspace="results/flux_pumped_resonator")
pump_axis = PumpAxis(id="pump", frequency=7.0 * u.GHz)
dc_bias = CurrentDrive(id="dc_bias", at="pump", mode=(0,))
pump_drive = CurrentDrive(id="pump_drive", at="pump", mode=(1,))

hb = run.solve(
    run.original,
    HBSolveSpec(
        pump_axes=(pump_axis,),
        drives=(dc_bias, pump_drive),
        frequencies=signal_grid,
        cases=(
            HBCaseSpec(id="unbiased", currents={}),
            HBCaseSpec(
                id="dc_only",
                currents={dc_bias: 120.0 * u.uA},
            ),
            HBCaseSpec(
                id="dc_pump",
                currents={
                    dc_bias: 120.0 * u.uA,
                    pump_drive: 0.4 * u.uA,
                },
            ),
        ),
        truncation=HBTruncation(
            pump_harmonics=(3,),
            modulation_harmonics=(1,),
            three_wave_mixing=True,
            four_wave_mixing=True,
        ),
    ),
)
```

`pump_axis`, `signal_grid`, and each `CurrentDrive` are ordinary Runtime
request objects defined by the
[HB drive/case contract](v1-runtime-contract.qmd#named-hb-drives-cases-and-mixing).
The cases bind DC and AC Fourier-current coefficients without mutating the
component or turning a drive current into a component parameter.

The physical coupling identity is
`M = k * sqrt(L1 * L2)`, with signed `k` supplying the V1 authoring authority.
The canonical orientation, energy, and passivity semantics remain in
[Inductive Coupling Coefficient, Mutual Inductance, and Self Inductance](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/quantum-circuits/inductive-coupling-coefficient-mutual-self-inductance.qmd).

## Direct and HB realization

The same Plan and component identities feed both backends:

| Component content | Direct | HB |
|---|---|---|
| R, L, C, scalar RLGC ladder | Linear physical rows | Corresponding linear rows |
| JJ | Explicit `L_J0` small-signal branch plus declared parallel `Cj` | Nonlinear Josephson row plus declared parallel `Cj` |
| Finite-loop SQUID | Both junctions linearized at their zero-phase, zero-bias `L_J0`, with loop and mutual coupling retained | Both nonlinear junctions, finite loop, and mutual pump coupling retained |

V1 Direct analysis does not accept an arbitrary supplied bias phase or claim a
finite-bias JJ/SQUID linearization. A future operating-point linearization must
define and evidence its bias solution before changing that contract.

JosephsonCircuits is an HB backend, not the topology authority. Its official
[flux-pumped JPA example](https://josephsoncircuits.org/stable/#Flux-pumped-Josephson-parametric-amplifier-(JPA))
shows the relevant two-junction, loop-inductor, pump-inductor, and mutual-coupling
path, while also describing flux-bias and three-wave-mixing support as
relatively untested. SCNSim preserves that limitation rather than expanding
the backend's guarantee.

## Parameter variants and derived mutual inductance

Every public factory parameter becomes a stable `ParameterRef` only when the
factory exposes it:

```python
candidate = ParameterSet({
    jpa.parameter("loop_inductance"): 44.0 * u.pH,
    pump_inductor.parameter("inductance"): 1.1 * u.nH,
})

result = run.solve(run.original, direct_spec, parameters=candidate)
```

After each ParameterSet is bound, SCNSim resolves both self inductances and
derives the mutual inductance from the signed coupling coefficient:

```text
M = k * sqrt(L1 * L2)
```

`k` must be finite and dimensionless with `abs(k) < 1`. It is the only public
mutual-coupling input in V1; the consumer cannot provide an independent `M`
that might disagree with the two bound self inductances. Each receipt records
branch orientations, `L1`, `L2`, `k`, derived `M`, and the exact backend
mapping.

For more than two coupled inductive branches, every pairwise `abs(k) < 1`
check is only necessary. Preflight assembles the complete reciprocal
inductance matrix after ParameterSet binding and requires it to be positive
definite for the declared independent finite branches. SCNSim rejects an
incompatible collection of individually plausible pairwise coefficients.

## Inspection and evidence

`run.explain(ref, spec).show()` performs the same deterministic component and
ParameterSet preflight used by execution, without launching a solver or
writing the workspace. For component authoring it shows:

- every Library exact identity and public component schema;
- composite hierarchy and primitive/backend expansion;
- component-pin to net/reference/port mapping;
- source units, canonical SI values, and public `ParameterRef` identities;
- Direct and HB realization of each expanded row;
- scalar RLGC source classification, canonical values, extraction frequency,
  and content-derived provenance, plus TL section count and bound section
  length;
- all three IDC capacitance branches;
- JJ and optional parallel `Cj` rows;
- both SQUID junction rows, their shared parameter refs, loop orientation, and
  loop branch; and
- coupled branch orientations, bound `L1` and `L2`, signed `k`, derived `M`,
  and backend mapping.

The same facts are sealed into terminal receipts. Inspection text is not a
second schema or a substitute for the machine-readable evidence.

## Failure contract

Plan seal or deterministic preflight fails before backend execution for:

- duplicate component, net, reference, or port IDs, or duplicate pin/public-
  parameter names inside one component schema;
- an unknown pin, parameter, inductive branch, net, or unbound/foreign Library
  instance;
- assigning one pin to different nets, incrementally redefining a net, or
  declaring other than one Plan reference;
- a port bound to the reference or an unknown net, or directly to a pin;
- a bare physical number, foreign Pint registry, non-finite Quantity, or
  dimensional mismatch;
- non-positive R, L, C, or `L_J0`; negative `Cj`; invalid scalar RLGC values;
  or a non-positive/non-integer `n_sections`;
- a missing, empty, malformed, or unsupported Q2D CSV; missing or repeated
  primary C/G/L/R matrix blocks; invalid per-length units or extraction
  frequency; inconsistent conductor labels/order; a matrix other than `1 x 1`;
  or non-finite/invalid parsed scalar values;
- a SQUID whose junction parameters are not shared or whose finite loop
  inductance is missing, non-finite, or non-positive;
- mutual coupling between branches from different Plans, a non-inductive or
  unknown branch, or missing branch orientation; and
- a coupling coefficient that is not a finite SCNSim-registry dimensionless
  Quantity or has `abs(k) >= 1`, or a complete bound inductance matrix that is
  not reciprocal positive definite.

Exact `0 * u.F` is the one valid zero for optional `junction_capacitance`.
Zero series resistance or conductance in an RLGC model may be valid when the
declared branch permits it; negative or non-finite values are not.

## Known V1 limits

- Component factories and sketches on this page are contracts, not an
  installable implementation.
- The transmission line is a scalar, uniform, fixed-section RLGC ladder.
- AEDT Q2D import accepts only one native scalar `1 x 1` combined `CG, RL`
  export and freezes its values at the recorded extraction frequency; it does
  not verify a solver receipt or create a frequency-dependent line.
- Symmetric SQUID factories do not expose junction asymmetry or arbitrary
  per-arm parameter injection.
- Direct JJ/SQUID analysis is limited to the declared zero-phase, zero-bias
  `L_J0` small-signal realization.
- JosephsonCircuits flux-pump and three-wave-mixing capability retains the
  upstream validation limitation described above.
- `LinearizedFloatingQubit` and `ReflectiveJPA` are not V1 built-ins; consumers
  build those circuits from the declared generic components.
- Component schematic rendering remains a projection of the original Plan,
  never topology authority.
